methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Aestus Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $10M+ to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public (277810.KQ) and eight private—including Series B-stage peers Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity, alongside earlier-stage reference points like Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods yield materially divergent results. The stage-progression method, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $10M raised proxy, implies a $20M valuation. The peer-median approach, based on four same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables, yields $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The $1.7B median reflects the typical Series B valuations of three peers but carries substantial upward bias from that cohort's stage advancement.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $17M to $2.0B, with a median of $860M. This wide band reflects a fundamental tension: the stage-progression method anchors to actual capital deployed, while peer medians conflate multiple stages and likely overweight more mature, higher-valued comparables. Key uncertainties include whether Aestus's technology trajectory and revenue traction justify the upper quartile of peer valuations or whether a Series A discount to the observed $1.1B–$2.0B range is more appropriate. Near-term revenue and customer validation metrics would materially narrow this band.
